# Platform.Storage.Cache.write()

Writes a "temporary" file to the cache.

## Syntax

<CodeBlock language="ts">
  <span style={{ display: 'inline' }}>SpotifyPlus.Platform.Storage.Cache.write(path: string, value: string | object | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer): void</span>
</CodeBlock>

## Examples

The following example shows how an extension can cache a search response for this extension.

```ts
// Cache a search response for this extension.
const query = 'After Hours';
const results = await SpotifyPlus.Search.search(query);

SpotifyPlus.Platform.Storage.Cache.write('search/after-hours.json', {
  query,
  items: results.items,
});

console.log(`Cached ${results.items.length} results`);
```

## Parameters

`path`

<Badge>string</Badge> <Badge variant="danger">Required</Badge>

A path relative to this extension’s storage area.

`value`

<Badge>string | object | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer</Badge> <Badge variant="danger">Required</Badge>

The value to store.

## Remarks

I put the quotes around "temporary" because Android almost never clears your cache. The only time Android will clear it is if the user clears it themself, or if you're running very low on storage.
